position: DHS headquarters offices (Management Directorate, OCFO, FPS, OPE, OPA, OLA)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Federal Protective Service report to the Secretary instead of through the Management Directorate, with information-sharing agreements with the Marshals, Park Police and FBI. It also recommends merging the Office of Partnership and Engagement into the Office of Public Affairs, moving congressional appropriations staff from the Chief Financial Officer's office into the Office of Legislative Affairs, and having component public and legislative affairs staff report to their headquarters counterparts.

status_summary: The FY2027 budget request, reported on 2026-04-03, proposes folding the Management Directorate, the Office of Intelligence and Analysis and the Office of Homeland Security Situational Awareness into the Office of the Secretary and Executive Management under one appropriation; CRS puts the consolidated request at about 4.67 billion dollars. The Federal Protective Service appears as a fee-funded line inside that consolidated entity (about 2.03 billion dollars), and neither the budget overview nor CRS describes a change to its reporting line. No merger of Partnership and Engagement into Public Affairs, and no move of appropriations staff into Legislative Affairs, was found.

timeline.event: Reporting on the FY2027 budget request described a proposal to combine the Management Directorate, Intelligence and Analysis, and related headquarters offices into one headquarters office, with a stated saving of 53 million dollars; it needs congressional approval.

title: Put FPS under the Secretary and merge DHS headquarters communications and budget offices
uncertainties: The budget overview copy prints no date and was read through a hosted copy; it has no narrative on FPS, only a table line. The 2026-04-03 date is that of the Defense One report on the request, as in c05-14; the request's own release date was not pinned. Moving FPS with the Management Directorate into the Office of the Secretary and Executive Management could be read as bringing FPS closer to the Secretary, but no source says FPS would report to the Secretary. The office merger and reporting-line items for Partnership and Engagement, Public Affairs and Legislative Affairs were not found in any source, which is absence of evidence from a limited search; the December 2025 Council notice was still issued by the Office of Partnership and Engagement. The Intelligence and Analysis, CRCL and Privacy items are covered by c05-14 and c05-15.
